object_description: elongated single-story building forming courtyard spaces
design_condition: The long building docks onto the existing pavilions, creates an atrium courtyard and a southeast-open U-shaped outdoor area, and extends the complex through a sequence of differently sized courtyards.

positive.statement: The precise placement preserves the delicate scale of the existing complex despite the large footprint.
The sequence of courtyard spaces is a congenial continuation of the original design idea.
The informal entrances and exits underline the openness of the complex.
The simple and intelligent structure uses structural resources economically without compromising tectonic expression.
The modular building structure opens considerable flexibility for future school use.
The delicately structured construction fits seamlessly into the existing complex through subtle differentiation and proportioning.
The horizontal juxtaposition of spatial functions offers an open and unconventional vessel with potential for a future school model.
The project has low construction costs compared with the other entries.

negative.statement: The concept can only be achieved by demolishing the protected break halls and abandoning their associated outdoor spaces and trees.
The alternating classrooms and group rooms make it difficult to create quiet niches for collaboration.
The high density of use in the central access corridor is unfavorable, especially during breaks.
The basement workrooms, lit only through a light shaft, do not offer enough quality of stay.
The location of the day school makes it difficult to oversee children playing on the school grounds.
The spatial proximity of the new rooms to younger children's outdoor areas risks distraction and disruption.
Achieving the energy standard requires complex constructions and a large photovoltaic system.
The arrangement of the spatial sequences inside and outside does not convincingly exploit the project's potential.
